title: Radiology Technician
description: Company Description Harare Central Hospital is a major public healthcare institution serving a diverse patient population with a wide range of medical and surgical services. The hospital provides essential diagnostic and treatment services, including radiology, to support quality, patient-centered care. As a teaching and referral hospital, it offers opportunities to work alongside experienced healthcare professionals and contribute to clinical training. Radiology staff play an important role in supporting timely diagnoses and improving patient outcomes within a busy, multidisciplinary environment. Role Description This full-time, on-site Radiology Technician role is based in Dire Dawa and involves performing diagnostic imaging procedures in accordance with established protocols and safety standards. The Radiology Technician will operate radiologic equipment to produce high-quality images, position patients accurately, and ensure proper use of radiation protection measures. Day-to-day responsibilities include reviewing imaging requests, preparing patients and rooms, maintaining equipment, and documenting procedures in patient records. The role also involves collaborating with radiologists, physicians, nurses, and other healthcare team members to support accurate diagnoses and prompt patient care. The Radiology Technician will follow hospital policies, adhere to infection control practices, and participate in ongoing training to maintain professional competencies. Qualifications Candidates should possess strong radiologic practice skills, including Radiologic Technology and Radiology, with the ability to perform standard diagnostic imaging procedures safely and accurately. Candidates should demonstrate solid knowledge of Radiation Safety, including proper shielding, dose monitoring, and adherence to regulatory and hospital safety protocols. Candidates should, where applicable, hold or be eligible for American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) certification, or equivalent recognized credentials for radiologic professionals. Candidates should have a sound understanding of Medicine as it relates to imaging indications, basic anatomy, and the clinical context of radiologic examinations. Diploma or degree in Radiologic Technology or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Current professional license or registration to practice as a Radiology Technician, in line with local regulatory requirements. Ability to communicate clearly with patients and colleagues, provide compassionate patient care, and work effectively within a multidisciplinary team. Attention to detail, reliability in following protocols, and willingness to work shifts, weekends, or on-call as required by hospital operations.

title: Coffee Grader - Quality Control
description: TORQ Commodities is a physical commodities trading and supply chain management company with vertically integrated operations across Asia, Africa, and Europe. With a focus on procurement, shipping, and logistics, the company works closely across origin and supply chain operations to maintain quality, consistency, and traceability. This role is focused on safeguarding coffee quality through disciplined grading, sensory evaluation, and cross-functional coordination. As Coffee Grader - Quality Control, you will play an important part in ensuring that supplier samples, assembled lots, and pre-shipment approvals meet agreed specifications while supporting reliable quality decisions across origin operations. Responsibilities Conduct physical coffee grading, cupping, sensory evaluation, moisture analysis, and defect analysis Assess supplier samples, assemble lots, approve pre-shipment samples, and verify origin traceability Coordinate with procurement teams, suppliers, processing facilities, and warehouses to maintain agreed quality standards Apply the relevant origin-specific technical focus and grading standards for the coffees handled in the assigned posting Requirements 5-7 years of experience in coffee grading and quality control, including at least 3 years in Côte d'Ivoire, Ethiopia, Uganda, or Vietnam 3-5 years of on-ground or direct B2B coffee sourcing experience, with 3-5 years of direct coordination with procurement teams, suppliers, processing facilities, and warehouses within coffee sourcing or origin operations Active Q Arabica Grader and Q Robusta Grader licences Strong knowledge of SCA/CQI physical and sensory evaluation protocols Hands-on ability to independently run cupping lab workflows, including sample roasting, grinding, brewing, sensory evaluation, and scoring Hands-on experience performing physical coffee grading, including moisture measurement, screen sizing, green coffee defect identification and counting, representative lot sampling, sample labelling, retention, and traceability Experience assessing consistency and assembling lots against specifications, aligning lot specifications, and communicating quality findings to procurement teams and suppliers Experience managing pre-shipment sample evaluations and approvals, ensuring dispatched lots match approved samples Experience resolving quality discrepancies using cupping results, defect analysis, and supporting records, including coordinating corrective actions such as sorting, reprocessing, or lot segregation Experience maintaining cupping scores, grading reports, and moisture and defect records in Excel, along with documentation of quality decisions and escalation of unresolved disputes Knowledge of regional processing methods, grading frameworks, and the ability to apply the relevant origin-specific grading standards Willingness to work in the assigned country and travel to sourcing locations
